title: GRS JSON document
description:
Terms:
GRS is GoodRelax Scheduler, which opens and edits a Schedule Document and reads and writes GRS JSON files, the format that this GRS JSON Schema defines.
MSPDI (Microsoft Project XML Data Interchange) is the XML file format that Microsoft Project uses. GRS can also read and write MSPDI (.xml) files.
"Same as MSPDI X" indicates that the property has the same meaning and values as MSPDI element X. The description of that property notes any GRS-specific difference.
Concepts:
WBS is the tree of parent and child tasks, as in MSPDI.
Task groups are GRS's own objects that let GRS draw several tasks in one Task Group Lane. Each task names exactly one task group in grs.taskGroupId.
An MSPDI object keeps the values that only GRS uses under the key grs of that object.
GRS counts working days using a single calendar: the calendar that project.calendarUid names.
Passthrough: GRS keeps the MSPDI values that GRS does not use in grs.passthrough of each object, and the MSPDI elements that GRS does not turn into objects in the passthrough lists; GRS writes both back to MSPDI unchanged.
Actual dates are the authoritative source of task progress. GRS decides from the actual dates of a task whether the task is not started, in progress, suspended, or finished. GRS recalculates percentComplete from those dates when GRS opens a GRS JSON file.
Delay Diagnostics: GRS never stores Delay Diagnostics results in a GRS JSON file, because a stored result goes out of date as soon as the Schedule Document changes.
When a person starts Delay Diagnostics or an AI agent asks for Delay Diagnostics, GRS calculates the results from the current Schedule Data and project.statusDate.
While GRS shows Delay Diagnostics results, GRS keeps those results and does not recalculate them.
The shape of GRS JSON:
$schema           Address of this schema
schemaVersionUtc  Version of the shape
buildVersionUtc   GRS build that wrote the file
documentStamp     Last change, last save and last editor
documentSettings  How GRS shows the schedule on opening
scheduleData      Schedule data
  +- head values: scheduleDataTimeZone, sourceFormat, importedTopTaskOutlineLevel, mspdiImportCount, highestIssuedUid
  +- same as MSPDI: project, calendars, passthroughCalendars, tasks, passthroughTasks, resources, passthroughResources, assignments, passthroughAssignments
  +- GRS only: taskGroups, baselineTasks, highlightBoxes, commentBoxes
changeLogEntries  Notes on changes
Omit a property that has no value: never write null or [].

$schema.title: Address of this schema
$schema.description: This value gives the address of the latest GRS schema; every document holds the same address.

schemaVersionUtc.title: Version of the shape
schemaVersionUtc.description: This value gives the UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of GRS JSON, meaning the keys and the rules, last changed.

buildVersionUtc.description: This value gives the UTC time when someone built the GRS program that wrote this file. This value serves debugging only; schemaVersionUtc tells whether GRS can read the file.
buildVersionUtc.title: GRS build that wrote the file

documentStamp.title: Last change, last save and last editor
documentStamp.description: This object holds the Document Stamp: when the Schedule Data and the Schedule Document last changed, when GRS last saved the file, and who last edited the Schedule Document.

documentSettings.title: How GRS shows the schedule on opening
documentSettings.description: This object holds the Document Settings: how GRS shows the Schedule Document when GRS opens the Schedule Document. GRS writes the keys from the widest effect to the narrowest.

displayScaleRatio.description: This value scales the Schedule Canvas as a ratio to the normal size. GRS multiplies the values of keys ending in Px by this ratio when drawing, and saves those values unscaled.

fontSizePreset.description: This value is the text size step of the Schedule Canvas. GRS holds the pixel size of each step, and displayScaleRatio scales that size.

isThemeMonochrome.description: GRS draws the theme in monochrome when this value is true. This value changes only the drawing; the colors saved in the Schedule Document stay the same.

themeHue.description: This value names the hue of the theme. Every color written as {"type": "theme"} takes this hue; GRS holds the hue angle of each name.

viewTimeZone.description: This object sets the Display Base Time Zone: the time zone in which GRS shows date-times on the Schedule Canvas and the Time Ruler.

type.description: "sameAsScheduleData": GRS shows date-times in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone and follows that time zone when the time zone changes. "fixed": GRS shows date-times at the offset in utcOffset.

utcOffset.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". This value gives the UTC offset in which GRS shows date-times, such as "+09:00". The offset is standard time; GRS never adds daylight saving time.

additionalTimeZones.description: This list holds the Additional Time Zones, clocks that GRS shows besides the Display Base Time Zone. While GRS shows times of day, each clock adds a row under the Time Ruler.

utcOffset.description: This value gives the UTC offset of this clock, such as "-04:00". The offset already includes any daylight saving time, and GRS uses the offset all year.

zoneNameType.description: This value picks the kind of zone name that GRS shows for this clock and does not change the offset. "standard": the standard-time name; "daylight": the daylight-time name.

isTimeOfDayVisible.description: GRS shows the time of day on the Schedule Canvas, for the whole Schedule Document, when this value is true. The saved date-times keep their time either way.

dayWidthPx.description: This value is the Day Width (the horizontal zoom): the width of one calendar day on the Time Ruler, in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1. Zoom to Fit sets this value.

fitDayRange.description: This object sets the Fit Span: the days that Zoom to Fit and PNG and SVG pictures show. This range does not limit which tasks GRS saves or writes to MSPDI.

type.description: "fixed": the Fit Span runs from firstDay to lastDay with no margin, and those two whole days touch the edges of the Task Group Lanes. "automatic": the Fit Span covers everything that GRS draws, plus a margin that GRS fixes and does not save; GRS keeps no firstDay or lastDay.

firstDay.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". This value gives the first day of the Fit Span (included), as a day in the Display Base Time Zone.

lastDay.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". This value gives the last day of the Fit Span; the Fit Span includes this whole day.

verticalZoom.description: This object holds the two values that one step of vertical zoom and Zoom to Fit change together. When this key is absent, GRS chooses both values as Zoom to Fit does.

ratio.description: This value gives the vertical size of the Task Graphics as a ratio to the default size: 2 draws Plan Bars, Actual Bars and Name Labels twice as tall.

automaticallyShownDepth.description: This value is the depth to which GRS shows task groups with showMode "automatic". A zoom-in step changes ratio only after this value reaches the deepest level; ratio never sets this value.

taskGroupPanelWidthPx.description: This value gives the width of the Task Group Panel, in CSS pixels when displayScaleRatio is 1.

isTaskGroupPanelWidthFixed.description: true: taskGroupPanelWidthPx sets the width of the Task Group Panel; false: a drag of the Panel Divider sets the width.

pinnedTaskGroupIds.description: This list holds the ids of the Pinned Task Groups, which stay at the top during vertical scrolling. A pin shows the task group at any depth if showMode is "automatic", never if "hidden".

taskPlacementDirection.description: This value sets the Placement Direction: how GRS stacks the overlapping tasks of one Task Group Lane on Stack Tiers, earliest task first; this value does not order the task groups. "bottomToTop": the earliest task goes on the lowest tier; "topToBottom": the earliest task goes on the top tier.

scrollPosition.description: This object says where the view of the Schedule Canvas starts when GRS opens the Schedule Document.

type.description: "automatic": nobody has chosen a place, so GRS chooses one on opening; this value does not mean today or the status date. "fixed": the four keys below give the place.

leftEdgeDay.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". This value gives the day at the left edge of the view.

leftEdgeDayOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "fixed". This value says how far the left edge lies to the right of the start of leftEdgeDay, in percent of one day; 0 is the start of the day.

topEdgeTaskGroupId.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". This value gives the id of the task group at the top edge of the view. When that task group no longer exists, GRS treats the scroll position as "automatic".

topEdgeTaskGroupOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "fixed". This value says how far the top edge lies below the top of that task group, not of the screen, in percent of the lane height plus the gap below.

scheduleCanvasElements.description: This object chooses which elements GRS draws on the Schedule Canvas: true draws the element, and false hides the element. GRS writes the keys in this order: bars, labels, lines.

isPlanBarVisible.description: GRS draws the Plan Bars when this value is true; isActualBarVisible controls the Actual Bars separately.

isActualBarVisible.description: GRS draws the Actual Bars when this value is true; isPlanBarVisible controls the Plan Bars separately.

isBaselineOutlineVisible.description: GRS draws the Baseline Outline when this value is true: the baseline (baselineTasks) drawn over the current tasks.

isAssigneeLabelVisible.description: GRS draws the Assignee Label of each task when this value is true.

isPercentCompleteLabelVisible.description: GRS draws the Percent Complete Label of each task when this value is true.

isProgressStatusMarkVisible.description: When this value is true, GRS draws the Resume Marks and the Progress Status Marks, which show progress status by shape past the Actual Bar end, not on the Progress Line.

isPlanDatesVisible.description: GRS draws the planned start and finish dates to the right of each Name Label when this value is true.

isDependencyLineVisible.description: GRS draws the Dependency Lines when this value is true.

isProgressLineVisible.description: GRS draws the Progress Line when this value is true: one zigzag line from the status date through the task progress point of each task.

isDateGridLinesVisible.description: GRS draws the Date Grid Lines when this value is true: vertical lines at each date.

isTaskGroupGridLinesVisible.description: GRS draws the Task Group Grid Lines when this value is true: horizontal lines between task groups, in the Task Group Lanes and in the Task Group Panel.

delayDiagnosisSettings.description: This object holds the settings of Delay Diagnostics that belong to the Schedule Document.

parentTaskProgressToleranceWorkingDays.description: This value gives the working days by which a parent's progress point may stray beyond the progress points below before Delay Diagnostics marks the parent doubtful. This value excuses no late finish.

tableWindows.description: This object holds the checks, column filters and sort of the tables in the Search Window, the Delay Diagnostics Report Window and the Resource List Window, but no window positions.

searchWindow.description: This object holds the table settings of the Search Window: the task table and the Comment Box table.

delayDiagnosisReportWindow.description: This object holds the table settings of the Delay Diagnostics Report Window.

resourceListWindow.description: This object holds the table settings of the Resource List Window.

scheduleData.description: This object holds the Schedule Data: five head values, then the MSPDI part, which GRS reads from and writes to MSPDI, then the GRS part, which only GRS defines.
scheduleData.title: Schedule data

scheduleDataTimeZone.description: This object gives the time zone of the date-times in scheduleData, which carry no offset; GRS does not write this zone to MSPDI. Record times such as documentStamp use UTC.

utcOffset.description: This value gives the fixed offset from UTC in standard time, and GRS never switches to daylight saving time. GRS refuses to open a file with an offset outside this list.

sourceFormat.description: This value says which format this Schedule Document came from, and GRS does not write this value to MSPDI. "grs": made in GRS; "mspdi12" and "mspdi15": an MSPDI file in the form of MS Project version 12 or 15.

importedTopTaskOutlineLevel.description: This value gives the MSPDI OutlineLevel of the top tasks in the imported file, not counting the project summary task; GRS gives this OutlineLevel to the top WBS tasks when writing MSPDI.

mspdiImportCount.description: This value counts the MSPDI imports into this Schedule Document. At each import, GRS adds 1 and copies the new value to grs.importOrigin.mspdiImportCountWhenLastIncluded of each imported task.

lastMspdiImport.description: This object records when GRS last imported an MSPDI file and the file name, and is absent before the first import. People and AI agents read this object; GRS compares mspdiImportCount instead.

importedAt.description: This value gives the UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when GRS imported the MSPDI file.

fileName.description: This value gives the name of the imported MSPDI file, such as "plan-v3.xml". GRS writes the file name only, never the folder, so that the file keeps no personal path.

highestIssuedUid.description: This value is the highest uid that GRS has issued, one counter for tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. GRS gives a new entity this value plus 1 and never reuses a uid.

project.description: Same as MSPDI Project. scheduleData.project holds only the values for the whole project: the MSPDI lists (calendars, tasks, resources, assignments) sit beside project in scheduleData, not inside project as in MSPDI.

calendars.description: Same as MSPDI Calendars. GRS counts every working day with the one calendar that project.calendarUid names; GRS keeps the other calendars only to write those calendars back to MSPDI.

passthroughCalendars.description: This list holds the whole MSPDI Calendar elements outside calendars[]. GRS writes each element back into MSPDI right after the calendar that precedingCalendarUid names.

precedingCalendarUid.description: This value is the uid of the nearest calendar in calendars[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

mspdiElement.description: This object holds the whole MSPDI element, keyed by the names of the child elements as in MSPDI. GRS writes the element back unchanged.

tasks.description: Same as MSPDI Tasks. The order of this list carries no meaning: parentTaskUid and siblingIndex give the WBS tree. GRS writes MSPDI tasks depth first along that tree and rebuilds ID, OutlineLevel, OutlineNumber and Summary.

passthroughTasks.description: This list holds the whole MSPDI Task elements outside tasks[], such as the project summary task, which GRS writes first. GRS writes each other element right after the task that precedingTaskUid names.

precedingTaskUid.description: This value is the uid of the nearest task in tasks[] that precedes this element in MSPDI, never a dependency predecessor. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

mspdiElement.description: This value is the whole MSPDI element, keyed by the names of the child elements as in MSPDI. GRS writes the element back unchanged.

resources.description: Same as MSPDI Resources. GRS lists the resources in the Resource List Window and shows the resources of each task in the Assignee Label.

passthroughResources.description: This list holds the whole MSPDI Resource elements outside resources[]. GRS writes each element back into MSPDI right after the resource that precedingResourceUid names.

precedingResourceUid.description: This value is the uid of the nearest resource in resources[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

mspdiElement.description: This value is the whole MSPDI element, keyed by the names of the child elements as in MSPDI. GRS writes the element back unchanged.

assignments.description: Same as MSPDI Assignments. Each item puts one resource on one task.

passthroughAssignments.description: This list holds the whole MSPDI Assignment elements outside assignments[]. GRS writes each element back into MSPDI right after the assignment that precedingAssignmentUid names.

precedingAssignmentUid.description: This value is the uid of the nearest assignment in assignments[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

mspdiElement.description: This value is the whole MSPDI element, keyed by the names of the child elements as in MSPDI. GRS writes the element back unchanged.

taskGroups.description: This list holds the task groups, depth first, as a tree of drawing rows separate from the WBS; GRS builds this list from the WBS when reading MSPDI.

baselineTasks.description: This list holds the baseline, a saved copy of earlier task dates. Baseline tasks hold no shape: each Baseline Outline takes the shape of the current task with the same uid.

highlightBoxes.description: This array holds the Highlight Boxes: rectangles in the Task Group Lanes that mark a range of days over a range of task groups.

commentBoxes.description: This array holds the Comment Boxes in the Task Group Lanes. The Leader Line of each Comment Box points at a task, a Highlight Box or a free point.

changeLogEntries.title: Notes on changes
changeLogEntries.description: This list holds the Change Log: notes that people or an AI write about changes to the Schedule Document, oldest first. GRS adds a new entry at the end.

Project.description: Same as MSPDI Project. GRS writes the keys in the order of the MSPDI schema, and the GRS part comes last under grs.

uid.description: Same as MSPDI UID. Before writing over another file, GRS treats that file as the same Schedule Document only when project.uid, project.name and the file name all match; an absent value never matches.

name.description: Same as MSPDI Name. GRS also uses the value, with project.uid and the file name, to tell whether an existing file holds the same Schedule Document.

title.description: Same as MSPDI Title. GRS shows the value as the Project Title in the App Header and builds the default file name in the Save As Dialog from the value.

author.description: Same as MSPDI Author. The author is not the last writer of the Schedule Document; documentStamp.lastEditedBy holds that writer.

creationDate.description: Same as MSPDI CreationDate. GRS writes the moment of creation when GRS makes a new Schedule Document.

revision.description: Same as MSPDI Revision. This value counts how many times the tool that made the MSPDI file saved the project; this value is not a GRS JSON version or a documentStamp time.

calendarUid.description: Same as MSPDI CalendarUID. GRS counts every working day with this calendar; without a valid value, GRS uses the first calendar with isBaseCalendar true, or else a built-in Monday-to-Friday calendar.

defaultStartTime.description: Same as MSPDI DefaultStartTime. GRS gives this time of day to a start that GRS sets by the day, and uses 08:00:00 when the key is absent. A milestone start takes defaultFinishTime instead.

defaultFinishTime.description: Same as MSPDI DefaultFinishTime. GRS gives this time of day to a finish that GRS sets by the day and to a milestone start, and uses 17:00:00 when the key is absent.

minutesPerDay.description: Same as MSPDI MinutesPerDay. This value gives the minutes in one working day (1d); GRS uses 480 when the key is absent, and warns on opening when the working times of a day total otherwise.

minutesPerWeek.description: Same as MSPDI MinutesPerWeek. The value gives the length of one working week in minutes.

daysPerMonth.description: Same as MSPDI DaysPerMonth. The value gives the number of working days in one month.

weekStartDay.description: Same as MSPDI WeekStartDay. Day-of-week code: 0=Sunday, 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, 4=Thursday, 5=Friday, 6=Saturday. Sunday is 0 here but 1 in calendars[].weekDays[].dayType. GRS starts each week of the Time Ruler on this day.

statusDate.description: Same as MSPDI StatusDate. GRS draws the Status Line at this date-time and runs Delay Diagnostics for this date. Without statusDate, GRS draws no Status Line and Delay Diagnostics does not run.

grs.description: This object is the GRS part of this project: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this project that GRS does not use and writes back to MSPDI unchanged.

Calendar.description: Same as MSPDI Calendar. GRS counts working days only with the calendar that project.calendarUid names.

isBaseCalendar.description: Same as MSPDI IsBaseCalendar. true marks a base calendar; false or no key means a calendar that is not a base calendar. MSPDI writes 1 or 0.

baseCalendarUid.description: Same as MSPDI BaseCalendarUID. This value names the calendar that this calendar inherits from in MSPDI. GRS writes this value back but does not inherit: GRS counts only the days that this calendar lists.

grs.description: This object is the GRS part of this calendar: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this calendar that GRS does not use and writes back unchanged. A whole Calendar element outside calendars[] goes to passthroughCalendars[].

weekDays.description: Same as MSPDI WeekDays. Each item describes the day of the week that dayType names.

exceptions.description: Same as MSPDI Exceptions. Each item is one exception: a day or a range of days that works differently from the days of the week, such as a holiday.

WeekDay.description: Same as MSPDI WeekDay. Each item gives the working state and the working times of one day of the week.

dayType.description: Same as MSPDI DayType. Day-of-week code: 1=Sunday, 2=Monday, 3=Tuesday, 4=Wednesday, 5=Thursday, 6=Friday, 7=Saturday. Sunday is 1 here but 0 in project.weekStartDay. GRS never uses the MSPDI code 0 (exception): calendars[].exceptions[] holds the exception days.

dayWorking.description: Same as MSPDI DayWorking. true means that the day of the week is a working day; false or no key means a non-working day. MSPDI writes 1 or 0.

grs.description: This object is the GRS part of this day of the week: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this day of the week that GRS does not use and writes back to MSPDI unchanged.

workingTimes.description: Same as MSPDI WorkingTimes. On a working day without workingTimes, GRS uses 08:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00.

Exception.description: Same as MSPDI Exception. This object gives a day or a range of days that works differently from the days of the week, such as a holiday; GRS counts only a one-off exception (see type).

fromDate.description: Same as MSPDI TimePeriod/FromDate. The value gives the first day of the exception. GRS reads only the date, and GRS writes T00:00:00 when GRS sets the date.

toDate.description: Same as MSPDI TimePeriod/ToDate. This value gives the last day of the exception, and the exception includes that day. GRS reads only the date, so T00:00:00 still counts the whole day; GRS writes T23:59:00.

dayWorking.description: Same as MSPDI DayWorking. true makes the days of the exception working days; false or no key makes those days non-working days, such as a holiday. MSPDI writes 1 or 0.

type.description: Same as MSPDI Type. This value gives the repeat code: 1=daily, 2=yearly on a day of the month, 3=yearly on a weekday position, 4=monthly on a day of the month, 5=monthly on a weekday position, 6=weekly, 7=by day count, 8=by weekday count, 9=no repeat. GRS counts the days of a one-off exception only (type 9, no type, or type 1 with period 1 or no period; a new exception takes 1) and keeps the others unchanged.

period.description: Same as MSPDI Period. This value gives the repeat interval for type, such as 2 with type 6 for every second week. GRS uses period only to tell whether a type 1 exception is one-off.

grs.description: This object is the GRS part of this exception: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this exception that GRS does not use and writes back to MSPDI unchanged.

workingTimes.description: Same as MSPDI WorkingTimes. On a working exception, these spans replace the spans of the day of the week; a working exception without workingTimes uses 08:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00.

WorkingTime.description: Same as MSPDI WorkingTime. This object is one span of working time within a day. GRS refuses overlapping spans in one day and spans that do not start before they end; touching spans are fine.

toTime.description: Same as MSPDI ToTime. 00:00:00 means 24:00, the end of the day.

Task.description: Same as MSPDI Task. GRS decides the progress status by these checks in order, and the first match wins: no actualStart, not started; actualFinish present, finished; resumeValid false, suspended with no resume date; resume present, suspended with a resume date; otherwise in progress.

start.description: Same as MSPDI Start. The value gives the planned start. GRS does not open a Schedule Document in which a task has no start.

finish.description: Same as MSPDI Finish. The value gives the planned finish; a milestone has the same start and finish. GRS does not open a Schedule Document in which a task has no finish.

stop.description: Same as MSPDI Stop. This value gives the date-time where the work so far stops on a task in progress or suspended. GRS removes stop when GRS finishes the task; actualFinish then holds the end.

resume.description: Same as MSPDI Resume. On a suspended task, the value gives the planned date-time when the remaining work restarts (work split in two parts).

resumeValid.description: Same as MSPDI ResumeValid. On a task with actualStart and no actualFinish, false means suspended with no resume date, and GRS ignores resume; no key is not false. GRS writes true with each resume date.

milestone.description: Same as MSPDI Milestone. This value is true for a milestone, and false or absent for a task with a span of work, though MSPDI writes 1 or 0.

percentComplete.description: Same as MSPDI PercentComplete. GRS recounts this value on opening: actual working time (actualStart to actualFinish or stop) over planned working time, times 100, rounded, uncapped. Without planned working time, the value is 100 after actualFinish, else 0.

actualStart.description: Same as MSPDI ActualStart. A task without actualStart has not started.

actualFinish.description: Same as MSPDI ActualFinish. Only a finished task has actualFinish; a percentComplete of 100 does not mean finished.

calendarUid.description: Same as MSPDI CalendarUID. The value names the calendar of this task alone. GRS keeps the value and writes the value back, but GRS counts working days with project.calendarUid only.

hyperlink.description: Same as MSPDI Hyperlink. The value is the title (display text) of the link, not the address; hyperlinkAddress holds the URL.

hyperlinkAddress.description: Same as MSPDI HyperlinkAddress. The value is the URL of the link; hyperlink holds the title.

parentTaskUid.description: This value is the uid of the parent task in the WBS, and a task without this key sits at the top. MSPDI has no such element.

siblingIndex.description: This value gives the place of this task among the tasks with the same parent, counted from 0. GRS writes 0, 1, 2 without gaps, reads the smallest first, and keeps array order on ties.

grs.description: This object holds the GRS values of this task. The keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names.

startSlopeCalendarDays.description: This value gives the Start Slope in calendar days: GRS slants the start edge of the Plan Bar to mark a start that is not firm, without changing the schedule.

finishSlopeCalendarDays.description: This value gives the Finish Slope in calendar days: GRS slants the finish edge of the Plan Bar to mark a finish that is not firm, without changing the schedule.

style.description: This object says how GRS draws the Task Graphic of this task: the shape, the fill and the stroke.

taskGroupId.description: This value is the id of the task group in whose Task Group Lane GRS draws this task; the task group is independent of the WBS parent (parentTaskUid).

importOrigin.description: This object records which MSPDI file and which task this task came from, for matching at later imports; a task made in GRS has no importOrigin.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this task that GRS does not use and writes back unchanged, except date-derived values such as Duration. A whole Task element outside tasks[] goes to passthroughTasks[].

predecessorLinks.description: Same as MSPDI PredecessorLink. Each item is one dependency: this task waits for one end of a predecessor task.

PredecessorLink.description: Same as MSPDI PredecessorLink. Each item makes the task that holds the item wait for one end of a predecessor task.

predecessorUid.description: Same as MSPDI PredecessorUID. The value is the uid of the predecessor task in tasks[].

type.description: Same as MSPDI Type. This value gives the link type code: 0=FF (finish-to-finish), 1=FS (finish-to-start), 2=SF (start-to-finish), 3=SS (start-to-start); the first letter names the end of the predecessor, and the second letter names the end of this task.

linkLag.description: Same as MSPDI LinkLag. The value gives the lag in tenths of a minute, whatever lagFormat says: 4800 is 480 minutes, one working day when project.minutesPerDay is 480. No key means no lag.

lagFormat.description: Same as MSPDI LagFormat. This value gives the unit code for showing the lag: 3=m, 4=em, 5=h, 6=eh, 7=d, 8=ed, 9=w, 10=ew, 11=mo, 12=emo, 19=%, 20=e%, 35=m?, 36=em?, 37=h?, 38=eh?, 39=d?, 40=ed?, 41=w?, 42=ew?, 43=mo?, 44=emo?, 51=%?, 52=e%? (m minutes, h hours, d days, w weeks, mo months, % percent, e elapsed time, ? estimated). The unit never changes linkLag; GRS counts the lag only for 3, 5 and 7, and for other codes only shows the lag.

grs.description: This object holds the GRS part of this link: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this link that GRS does not use and writes back to MSPDI unchanged.

ImportOrigin.description: This object records which MSPDI file and task an imported task came from, so that a later import of that file updates the task rather than adding a copy.

sourceProjectUid.description: This value is the Project UID of the MSPDI file that GRS imported this task from; when that file had no Project UID, the key is absent and importSessionId identifies the file.

sourceTaskUid.description: This value is the UID of this task in that MSPDI file. The value can differ from uid, because GRS may give the imported task a new uid.

importSessionId.description: This value is the id that GRS made for the import that brought this task in. This id stands in for sourceProjectUid when the MSPDI file had no Project UID.

mspdiImportCountWhenLastIncluded.description: This value copies scheduleData.mspdiImportCount at the last import whose file contained this task. A value below the current count means that the latest import left this task out.

type.description: Same as MSPDI Type. Resource type code: 0=material, 1=work. Every resource has the same keys, whatever the code.

isCostResource.description: Same as MSPDI IsCostResource. true means a cost resource; false or no key means not a cost resource. MSPDI writes 1 or 0.

calendarUid.description: Same as MSPDI CalendarUID. The value names the calendar of this resource alone. GRS keeps the value and writes the value back, but GRS counts working days with project.calendarUid only.

grs.description: This object holds the GRS part of this resource: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this resource that GRS does not use and writes back unchanged. A whole Resource element outside resources[] goes to passthroughResources[].

taskUid.description: Same as MSPDI TaskUID. The value is the uid of the task in tasks[].

resourceUid.description: Same as MSPDI ResourceUID. The value is the uid of the resource in resources[].

grs.description: This object holds the GRS part of this assignment: the keys under grs are GRS names, not MSPDI element names. Here grs holds only passthrough.

passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI values of this assignment that GRS does not use and writes back unchanged. A whole Assignment element outside assignments[] goes to passthroughAssignments[].

TaskGroup.description: This object is a task group: one Task Group Lane and one row of the Task Group Panel. Task groups form a tree apart from the WBS and never go to MSPDI.

id.description: This value is the id of the task group, a random UUID.

name.description: This value is the task group name that the Task Group Panel shows. When the key is absent, the task group has no name and GRS shows an empty title.

parentTaskGroupId.description: This value is the id of the parent task group. When the key is absent, the task group is a top-level task group (depth 1).

siblingIndex.description: This value gives the place of this task group among the task groups with the same parent, counted from 0. GRS lists the task groups from the smallest value at the top.

style.description: This object tells GRS how to draw the task group (type TaskGroupStyle).

minHeightPx.description: This value is the minimum height of the Task Group Lane in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1; vertical zoom does not change this height. No key means no minimum.

representativeTaskUid.description: This value is the uid of the WBS task that this task group stands for. When a person nests this task group under another, GRS moves that task in the WBS to match.

hyperlinkAddress.description: This value is the URL that the task group links to. When the key is absent, the task group has no link.

hyperlink.description: This value is the title of the task group link, not the address. When the key is absent, the link has no title.

showMode.description: This value records what a person wants for this task group. "shown": GRS draws the task group at any depth unless an ancestor hides the task group. "hidden": GRS hides the task group and every task group below, even on zoom or Zoom to Fit, until a person shows the task group again. "automatic": GRS decides from automaticallyShownDepth, the pins and the path to a shown task group below. "hiddenUntilZoomIn": GRS hides the task group and every task group below until the next vertical zoom-in, and then changes the value to "automatic".

allowedEditorGroupName.description: This value names the group of people allowed to edit the tasks in this task group. GRS treats those tasks as read-only and refuses moves into a task group with another value.

BaselineTask.description: This object is one baseline task, which GRS draws only as a Baseline Outline over the current task with the same uid.

uid.description: This value is the uid of the current task that this baseline task belongs to.

name.description: This value is the task name at the time of the baseline.

start.description: This value is the planned start at the time of the baseline.

finish.description: This value is the planned finish at the time of the baseline.

milestone.description: This value records whether the task was a milestone at the time of the baseline; GRS still draws the outline in the shape of the current task.

HighlightBox.description: This object is one Highlight Box: a rectangle over a range of days and a range of task groups.

id.description: This value is the id of the Highlight Box, a random UUID.

style.description: This object tells GRS how to draw the Highlight Box (type HighlightBoxStyle).

firstDay.description: This value is the first day that the Highlight Box covers (included), as a day in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

lastDay.description: This value is the last day that the Highlight Box covers (included).

firstTaskGroupId.description: This value is the id of the first task group that the Highlight Box covers; the box covers every task group through lastTaskGroupId in task group tree order, both ends included.

lastTaskGroupId.description: This value is the id of the last task group that the Highlight Box covers (included).

CommentBox.description: This object is one Comment Box: a text box with a Leader Line, whose end (the Leader Anchor) stands at a free point, a task or a Highlight Box.

id.description: This value is the id of the Comment Box, a random UUID.

text.description: This value is the text of the Comment Box. When the key is absent, the Comment Box has an empty body.

style.description: This object tells GRS how to draw the Comment Box (type CommentBoxStyle).

leaderTarget.description: This object tells where the Leader Line of the Comment Box points. A deleted target becomes a free point; for a target missing from the file, GRS draws no Leader Line.

bodyOffsetPx.description: This object is the offset from the Leader Anchor to the lower-left corner of the Comment Box body, in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1; the zoom does not change this offset.

dx.description: This value is the horizontal part of the offset; a positive value moves the box to the right.

dy.description: This value is the vertical part of the offset; a positive value moves the box down.

hyperlinkAddress.description: This value is the URL that the Comment Box links to. When the key is absent, the Comment Box has no link.

hyperlink.description: This value is the title of the Comment Box link, not the address. When the key is absent, the link has no title.

type.description: "freePoint": the Leader Anchor stands at a place tied to nothing; "task": the Leader Anchor stands at one of eight points of the Plan Bar, the Actual Bar or the Milestone Mark of a task; "highlightBox": the Leader Anchor stands at one of eight points of a Highlight Box.

dateTime.description: Only when type is "freePoint". This value is the point in time where the Leader Anchor stands, as a date-time in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

taskGroupId.description: Only when type is "freePoint". This value is the id of the task group whose Task Group Lane holds the Leader Anchor.

taskGroupTopOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "freePoint". This value tells how far the Leader Anchor lies below the top edge of that Task Group Lane, in percent of the lane height; 100 is the bottom edge.

taskUid.description: Only when type is "task". This value is the uid of the task that the Leader Anchor snaps to.

snapPart.description: Only when type is "task". This value names the part of the Task Graphic that the Leader Anchor snaps to: "planBar" (the Plan Bar), "actualBar" (the Actual Bar) or "milestoneMark" (the Milestone Mark).

highlightBoxId.description: Only when type is "highlightBox". This value is the id of the Highlight Box that the Leader Anchor snaps to.

snapPoint.description: Only when type is "task" or "highlightBox". This value names the point of the target that the Leader Anchor snaps to: a corner or the middle of a side.

DocumentStamp.description: This object is the Document Stamp: the last change, the last save and the last editor. The Agent API uses this stamp to refuse writes based on an old read.

scheduleDataUpdatedAt.description: This value gives the time in UTC when the Schedule Data last changed. A change of documentSettings alone does not move this time.

documentUpdatedAt.description: This value gives the time in UTC when the Schedule Document last changed, whether in the Schedule Data or in documentSettings.

fileSavedAt.description: This value gives the time in UTC when GRS last saved the Schedule Document to a file. The key is absent until the first save.

lastEditedBy.description: This object says who last edited the Schedule Document. GRS always writes this key, also in a Schedule Document that nobody has edited yet.

Editor.description: This object tells who edited a Schedule Document: a person, an AI, or nobody yet; type chooses the case.

type.description: "user": a person edited the Schedule Document on the screen. "agent": an AI edited the Schedule Document through the Agent API. "template": nobody has edited yet, so the Schedule Document is still the template that comes with GRS.

name.description: This value gives the name of the editor: for "agent", the name that the AI reports; for "user", the name of the person, only when GRS knows the name.

ChangeLogEntry.description: This object is one note about a change to the Schedule Document, written by a person or an AI: when, who, which part, what, why, and anything else.

changedAt.description: This value gives the time in UTC when the change happened. GRS fills in the time when GRS adds the entry; a person may change the time later.

changedBy.description: This object says who made the change: the kind of editor and the name.

editorType.description: This value gives the kind of editor that wrote this entry, and GRS fills in the value. "user": a person wrote the entry on the screen; "agent": an AI wrote the entry through the Agent API.

name.description: This value gives the name of the editor: the name that a person typed, or the name that an AI reported.

affectedArea.description: This free text names the part of the Schedule Document that the change touched, for example "tasks" or the name of one task.

changeDescription.description: This free text says what changed.

reason.description: This free text gives the reason for the change.

remarks.description: This free text holds anything else about the change that the other keys do not hold.

Uid.description: This integer identifies an entity that comes from MSPDI (MSPDI UID), unique within one array; GRS never reuses a uid, and project.uid is a string instead.

Uuid.description: This string is a random lowercase UUID. GRS uses a UUID as the id of an object that only GRS defines, so that objects made apart never share an id.

Day.description: This string is a date without a time of day, in the time zone that each key names where that matters. A range of days (firstDay to lastDay) includes both ends.

Time.description: This string is a time of day without a date, written HH:MM:SS, as MSPDI writes a time.

DateTime.description: This string is a local date and time in scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone with no offset, as MSPDI writes a date-time. GRS reads the value to the minute and ignores the seconds.

UtcInstant.description: This string is a point in time in UTC, to the second. GRS uses this type for records, such as the Document Stamp, and for the two versions at the root.

StandardUtcOffset.description: This string is a fixed offset from UTC, such as "+09:00"; UTC itself is "+00:00". GRS uses the offset all year and never adds daylight saving time.

MspdiValue.description: This value is one MSPDI value: a string or a number for a text-only element, an array for a repeatable element (even with one item), or an object keyed by child element names. A boolean stays 0 or 1, as in MSPDI.

Passthrough.description: This object holds the MSPDI child elements of one entity that GRS does not use, keyed by element name. GRS writes them back unchanged in MSPDI schema order, repeats in array order.

MspdiElement.description: This object is one whole MSPDI element that GRS does not hold as an entity, keyed by child element names, such as the project summary task. GRS writes the element back unchanged.

hexColor.description: This value is the color as # and six lowercase hexadecimal digits (#rrggbb).

isCalculatedFromOppositeColorScheme.description: This value marks a side that GRS calculated from the opposite side, as a record of origin and not a switch; a side that a person chose lacks this key.

Color.description: This object is a color of type "theme", "palette" or "custom". Where a color key may be absent, an absent color means that GRS draws no fill or line there.

type.description: "theme": GRS takes the theme color for the place that holds this color, in the hue of documentSettings.themeHue; "palette": the color is one of the ten palette colors, named in name; "custom": light and dark hold the colors for the light and dark themes.

name.description: Only when type is "palette". This value names the palette color. Each name says how the color looks in the light theme; in the dark theme GRS keeps the hue and inverts the lightness.

light.description: Only when type is "custom". This object is the color for the light theme.

dark.description: Only when type is "custom". This object is the color for the dark theme, in the same shape as light.

TaskGroupColor.description: This value is the color of a Task Group Lane. This value has the same shape as Color, except that the palette color "black" is not allowed.

Paint.description: This object is a fill: a color and an opacity.

color.description: This value is the color of the fill (type Color).

opacityPercent.description: This value is the opacity of the fill in percent: 100 is solid, and at 0 GRS draws no fill.

Stroke.description: This object is a line: a color, an opacity and a width. To draw no line, leave out the whole stroke key.

color.description: This value is the color of the line (type Color).

opacityPercent.description: This value is the opacity of the line in percent: 100 is solid, and at 0 GRS draws no line.

widthPx.description: This value is the width of the line, in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1. The zoom does not change this width.

ShapeStyle.description: This object holds the fill and the outline of a shape. TaskStyle, HighlightBoxStyle and CommentBoxStyle all use this object.

fill.description: This value is the fill of the shape (type Paint). When the key is absent, GRS draws no fill.

stroke.description: This value is the outline of the shape (type Stroke). When the key is absent, GRS draws no outline.

TaskStyle.description: This object tells how GRS draws the Task Graphic of one task: the shape, the Plan Bar fill and the bar outline. A milestone uses milestoneShape; any other task uses taskShape.

taskShape.description: This value gives the shape of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar of a task that is not a milestone. "rectangle"; "chevron": a bar with a notched start and a pointed finish; "arrow"; "dumbbell": a thin line with a dot at each end.

milestoneShape.description: This value gives the shape of the Milestone Mark, and each value names the picture that GRS draws, for example diamond or star. Only a milestone has milestoneShape.

fill.description: This object sets the fill of the Plan Bar, and GRS fills the Actual Bar from the same color. No key means no fill; fill and stroke cannot both be absent.

stroke.description: This object sets the outline of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar. No key means no outline.

TaskGroupStyle.description: This object tells how GRS draws one task group: the color of the Task Group Lane.

color.description: This value is the color of the Task Group Lane: no key means no color, and {"type": "theme"} draws the theme color.

HighlightBoxStyle.description: This object tells how GRS draws one Highlight Box: the corner radius, the fill and the outline.

cornerRadiusPx.description: This value is the corner radius of the Highlight Box, in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1; 0 gives square corners.

fill.description: This value is the fill of the Highlight Box (type Paint). The fill always has a color; opacityPercent 0 makes the fill invisible.

stroke.description: This value is the outline of the Highlight Box (type Stroke). When the key is absent, GRS draws no outline.

CommentBoxStyle.description: This object tells how GRS draws one Comment Box: the fill of the body, the outline of the box and the Leader Line, and the text.

fill.description: This value is the fill of the Comment Box body (type Paint). The fill always has a color; opacityPercent 0 makes the fill invisible.

stroke.description: This value is the outline of the Comment Box and the Leader Line (type Stroke). When the key is absent, GRS draws no outline and no Leader Line.

font.description: This object holds the look of the Comment Box text: the color and the size.

color.description: This value is the color of the Comment Box text (type Color).

sizePx.description: This value is the size of the Comment Box text, in CSS pixels at displayScaleRatio 1. The zoom does not change this size.

ColumnFilter.description: This object is a filter on one column of a table; type chooses a filter by values or by a range of days.

type.description: "values": GRS hides the rows that show one of hiddenValues, and the empty rows when isBlankHidden is true; "dateRange": GRS hides the rows whose date lies outside firstDay to lastDay.

column.description: This value names the column by the content that the column shows, and the same name means the same content in every table. Search Window, task table: "progressStatus", "percentComplete", "taskType", "taskName", "resourceNames", "start", "finish", "actualStart", "actualFinish", "taskGroupPath" (the path from the top level). Search Window, Comment Box table: "text", "taskGroupName" (the task group of the Leader Anchor), "leaderTargetDay" (the day of the Leader Anchor). Delay Diagnostics Report Window: "diagnosisStatus", "percentComplete", "taskType", "taskName", "resourceNames", "planDates", "actualDates", "diagnosisReason". Resource List Window: "resourceSelectionStatus", "resourceName", "assignedTaskCount", "assignedTaskNames".

hiddenValues.description: Only when type is "values". This list holds the values whose rows the filter hides: the English status name for a status column, and the cell text as the table shows the text for any other column. "progressStatus": "notStarted", "inProgress", "suspendedWithResumeDate", "suspendedWithoutResumeDate", "finished", "delay", "unreliable", "bottleneck", "bottleneckPath"; "diagnosisStatus": "unreliable", "suspicion", "omission", "bottleneck", "bottleneckPath", "delay", "finishedDelayContribution"; "taskType": "task", "milestone"; "resourceSelectionStatus": "selected", "notSelected".

isBlankHidden.description: Only when type is "values". This value tells whether the filter hides the rows with an empty cell in this column.

firstDay.description: Only when type is "dateRange". This value is the first day that the filter keeps (included), as a day in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

lastDay.description: Only when type is "dateRange". This value is the last day that the filter keeps (included).

ColumnSort.description: This object tells how GRS sorts a table: by one column, in one direction.

column.description: This value names the column that GRS sorts the table by, with the same names as ColumnFilter.column.

direction.description: "ascending": GRS sorts from the smallest value to the largest; "descending": GRS sorts from the largest value to the smallest.

TaskTableWindow.description: This object tells how GRS shows a table of tasks (the Search Window or the Delay Diagnostics Report Window): the checks, the column filters and the sort.

isScheduleFilteredByChecks.description: This value turns Filter Schedule by Checks on or off: when true, GRS draws on the Schedule Canvas only the tasks checked in this table. The table itself keeps every row.

checkedTaskUids.description: This array lists the uids of the tasks whose row has a check in the Visibility column of this table. When the key is absent, no row has a check.

columnFilters.description: This array holds the column filters of this table, one for each filtered column. When the key is absent, no column has a filter.

columnSort.description: This object is the sort of this table: the column and the direction. When the key is absent, GRS shows the rows in the default order.

ResourceTableWindow.description: This object tells how GRS shows the table of the Resource List Window: the checks, the column filters and the sort.

isScheduleFilteredByChecks.description: This value turns Filter Schedule by Checks on or off: when true, GRS draws on the Schedule Canvas only the tasks of checked resources, plus unassigned tasks when isUnassignedChecked is true.

isUnassignedChecked.description: This value tells whether the "(no assignee)" row of the Resource List Window has a check.

checkedResourceUids.description: This list holds the uids of the resources whose row has a check in the Visibility column of the Resource List Window.

columnFilters.description: This array holds the column filters of this table, one for each filtered column. When the key is absent, no column has a filter.

columnSort.description: This object is the sort of this table: the column and the direction. When the key is absent, GRS shows the rows in the default order.
